result.reason: The passage is Ravina's argument to Rav Ashi that the court's stipulation must have addressed eating korban meat (not burning), using the 'hashta l'Yisrael yahvina le-Kohanim lo yahvina' logic — exactly what candidate 1 'Ravina's Q' describes.

All four items are the baraita debating whether salt must come from the donor's own home (like levona) or from communal supplies (like wood), which is precisely what candidate 2 'Baraita Proof' describes in its prose.
The passage discusses the meaning of 'morigim' and the threshing sledge, which directly matches the 'Morag' section's prose about Ulla, Rav Yehuda, and Rav Yosef explaining the threshing implement.

The passage is the Mishna stating the basic rule that a kometz mixed with another kometz or with priestly/libation meal offerings is fit, which is precisely what candidate 0's prose describes and analyzes.

The passage is Rabbi Yehuda's ruling about the minchat kohen mashiach and minchat nesachim being pesulah due to thick/thin consistency differences, which is precisely what the 'RY Thick/Thin' prose section discusses.

The passage is the Gemara source text covering all three cases (blood+water, blood+wine, blood+animal blood) plus Rabbi Yehuda's view, and it belongs under the first heading 'Blood Water' which introduces this entire Mishna from Zevachim — the subsequent headings discuss individual sub-topics derived from this single quoted passage.

All three items are part of Rabbi Yoḥanan's explanation of how both the Rabbis and Rabbi Yehuda derive their positions from the same Yom Kippur verse (ve-lakach mi-dam ha-par u-mi-dam ha-sa'ir), which is precisely what the 'YK Blood' prose describes.

All five items are the Gemara's debate about which feature (olin or min be-mino) drives the non-nullification principle, including the back-and-forth challenges and 'kashya' concessions — exactly what candidate 2 ('Feature Debate') describes in its prose.

The passage is precisely the Gemara's objection that when the mixtures absorb from each other it is 'min be-mino' so why does it matter — which is exactly what the prose of candidate 2 ('Similar Mix Q') describes and analyzes.

The passage contains Rava's statement about Rabbi Yehuda's principle of disregarding like-substance and nullification by unlike substance, which is precisely what the 'Flour Nulls' section's prose explains and analyzes.
